rules: Return the set of currently effective, explicitly requested supported actions in the complete utterance. Sort by fixed label ID and deduplicate repetitions. With no supported request, return an empty array []. Never add OTHER.

Page labels open a page or show its default existing information. They do not start recording a workout, measure heart rate, create an alarm, start a countdown, start a stopwatch, start navigation, or play music.

Do not discard explicit time, place, route, activity, song, or other execution parameters to force an unsupported request into a supported page label. A separate explicit request to open the page is still supported.

A prohibition such as 'do not turn on Bluetooth' does not imply the inverse action CLOSE_BLUETOOTH. Mentioned, quoted, hypothetical, conditional-on-an-unmet-event, or past actions are not present commands.

Resolve cancellation and self-correction by their explicit scope. 'Open Bluetooth; forget it' is []; 'Open Bluetooth; no, turn it off' is [CLOSE_BLUETOOTH]. A scoped withdrawal only removes the withdrawn request.
A clear sequence such as 'turn Bluetooth on, then turn it off' requests both action types. Keep both labels; this classifier does not encode sequence, arguments, or executability.
Requests for explanations, recommendations, how-to instructions, feature capabilities, or on/off status do not execute operations and receive no corresponding action label.
Unspecified references such as 'open that' without resolving context receive []. Do not invent missing objects or rely on previous conversation turns.
For mixed supported and unsupported requests, keep all and only the supported requests. For example, 'Open Bluetooth and set an alarm for seven' is [OPEN_BLUETOOTH].
Polite interrogative forms that actually request an operation, such as 'Could you turn on Bluetooth?', are supported commands. Distinguish them from explanatory and status questions.
Examples marked negative have no labels as standalone utterances. They define boundaries, not phrases that must be copied. Generate natural native English, Simplified Chinese, or Thai.
